summary: All 20 units (9 modules) were read in full. Every numeric key was recomputed and is correct, including herd immunity thresholds (87.5%, 93.75%), vaccine efficacy (90%), SVR (400), MAP shortfall (14.3), D-value times (18 min), NEWS2 totals (9, 11, 18), urine output (0.4 mL/kg/h), doubling times, attack rates and rates per device-day. The NEWS2-style bands match the published NEWS2 Scale 1 table, and the Sepsis-3 cut-offs (SOFA rise of 2 or more, MAP of at least 65 mmHg, lactate above 2 mmol/L) are stated correctly. No wrong answer keys, unsafe guidance or dose advice were found. The issues are minor: a few imprecise statements, one possibly dated vaccine claim, and some ambiguous wording. This is an AI review only. The course still needs a subject-matter expert before clinical reliance.

issues.problem: Table row 'Vaccine ... No effective vaccine (antigenic variation)' for N. gonorrhoeae. Some national programmes have recently begun using the meningococcal group B vaccine (4CMenB) for partial protection against gonorrhoea, so an absolute statement may be out of date. This is unverified.
issues.suggestedFix: Check current national guidance. Reword to something like 'no gonorrhoea-specific vaccine; meningococcal B vaccine gives partial cross-protection in some programmes'.

issues.problem: Hepatitis D row: 'Chronic when co-infection or superinfection on chronic HBV'. This blurs two situations. Co-infection with HBV usually resolves, and superinfection of a chronic HBV carrier usually becomes chronic.
issues.suggestedFix: State that HDV superinfection of a chronic HBV carrier usually becomes chronic, whereas simultaneous co-infection is usually self-limiting.

issues.problem: 'how many phage particles are released in total at the end of the third lytic cycle'. The key (120^3 = 1 728 000) is the number released in the third round only. 'In total' could be read as cumulative (about 1 742 520), which is outside the tolerance.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword to 'how many phage particles are released in the third round of lysis' or 'how many phage particles are present after the third lysis'.

issues.problem: The Spaulding table lists 'urinary catheters on insertion' as a Critical item needing sterilisation. Urinary catheters contact mucosa and are usually classed semi-critical (supplied sterile for single use). The cystoscope marking guide also hedges between semi-critical and sterilisation-preferred.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the catheter example or note that it is semi-critical but used sterile. Align the cystoscope wording with the table's semi-critical definition.

issues.problem: Titre written as '1:1 280' (thousands separator inside a ratio) can be misread as 1:1 and 280.
The NNT formula and question q007 (NNT from a prophylaxis trial) do not map to any stated objective for this unit (tissue involved, at-risk groups, azole and polyene mechanisms).
issues.suggestedFix: Add an evidence-interpretation objective or move NNT to an epidemiology or statistics unit.

issues.problem: Doubling-time worked example says 'Weekly reported cases rise from 50 to 400 over 9 days', which mixes weekly and daily counts. q007 uses 'daily reported cases'.
issues.suggestedFix: Say 'Reported cases rise from 50 to 400 over 9 days'.
